_note: Append-only. One entry per accepted release or reviewed amendment; one change item per agent-relevant semantic change. Entries carry NO commit identifier — a consumer derives the introducing commit from Git history at the target OID. Historical entries are never rewritten; a correction ships as a new amendment entry. Authoring rules: docs/release-ledger-authoring-guide.md.

entries.agent_impact: A consumer may now assemble a campaigns-os-tooling-orientation/v1 envelope from Git objects at a resolved commit, without executing anything from this repository. Nothing existing changed shape; adoption is optional and additive.

changes.summary: CI now runs the release-ledger completeness gate with --base on every pull request; npm run check runs only the structural half, because completeness needs a comparison point.

The agent entry point was introduced: canonical reading order, the supported-versus-internal boundary, mixed-version rules, and the rule that a consumer never executes target code to decide whether to trust the target.
The single machine-readable definition of an agent-relevant change was introduced: ten semantic classes, an ordered total classifier, and a stated reason for every exclusion.
A validated example orientation envelope for the current terminal outcome was introduced, generated from the contract rather than hand-written.
A validated example orientation envelope for the freshness_unknown terminal outcome was introduced, generated from the contract rather than hand-written.
A validated example orientation envelope for the legacy_baseline terminal outcome was introduced, generated from the contract rather than hand-written.
A validated example orientation envelope for the orientation_available terminal outcome was introduced, generated from the contract rather than hand-written.
A validated example orientation envelope for the recovered_interrupted_update terminal outcome was introduced, generated from the contract rather than hand-written.
A validated example orientation envelope for the refused terminal outcome was introduced, generated from the contract rather than hand-written.
A validated example orientation envelope for the restart_required terminal outcome was introduced, generated from the contract rather than hand-written.
A validated example orientation envelope for the updated terminal outcome was introduced, generated from the contract rather than hand-written.

Versioned bounds on an orientation read were introduced: source bytes, section count, section bytes, envelope bytes, and ledger entries. Exceeding one refuses with orientation_too_large; nothing is truncated.
The stable reason-code vocabulary was introduced, with one meaning, one deterministic remedy, one owning test id, and the terminal outcomes it may accompany per code.
surface_version advanced to 1.14.0; two orientation schemas were added as hashed entries and twenty-seven orientation contract, documentation, and fixture paths as named entries.
The normative orientation reference was introduced. It is generated from the contract files and fixtures, so a stale copy fails CI rather than misleading a reader.
The release-ledger authoring guide was introduced: what counts as agent-relevant, how a same-surface change is recorded, how an amendment works, and the full pass/fail matrix.
The compatibility promise now covers the orientation contract and its fixtures, and the change procedure now requires a release-ledger entry.
The orientation, ledger, change-policy, reason-code, and limits version lines were declared alongside the existing contract versions.
AGENTS.md and CHANGELOG.md were added to files[] so the new named surface actually ships, and the release-ledger and generated-documentation gates were added to npm run check.

The append-only release-ledger schema was introduced. It accepts unknown additive fields for producer-first rollout while required fields, known types, and safety-critical enums remain strict; custom validation still rejects commit-shaped entry properties.

The orientation envelope schema was introduced: ten required semantic groups, eight terminal outcomes, and the stable reason-code enum. It accepts unknown additive fields while keeping schema IDs, required fields, known types, and safety-critical enums strict.

entries.agent_impact: The QA Verdict and its committed sidecar projection now have hashed schema files a consumer can validate against, and the trust semantics of readback records are documented: trusted/trust_level/verified_at are receiver-stamped, trusted: false marks an anonymous submission, and every readback consumer must filter or segregate untrusted records. run-record verdict inference and sidecar promotion now enforce that segregation. Nothing existing changed shape; adoption is optional and additive.

changes.summary: The full QA verdict schema was introduced (contract identity campaigns-os-qa-verdict/v0; emitted schema_version literal "1.0"), derived from the emitting code and validated against real emitted verdicts. It documents the receiver-stamped trust fields and requires consumers to tolerate unknown additive fields.

The committed qa-verdict.json sidecar projection schema was introduced: same "1.0" schema_version literal as the full verdict, with the projection guarantees pinned — generated_at, emptied URL-bearing fields, the per-assertion allowlist, and the impossibility of receiver trust stamps.
surface_version advanced to 1.15.0; the QA verdict and sidecar-projection schemas were added as hashed entries.
The schema catalog enumeration now names the QA Verdict and its sidecar projection.
The QA Verdict and sidecar-projection version lines were declared, including the rule that the emitted schema_version literal stays "1.0" and cannot change without a breaking shape change.

A Verdict schema and trust semantics section was added: what trusted: false means (an anonymous, unattributed submission), that shape validity is not trust, and that every downstream readback consumer must filter on trusted or segregate untrusted records.

run-record automatic QA-verdict inference now excludes records stamped trusted: false, and qa promote refuses to project an untrusted source verdict into the committed sidecar; an operator-explicit --qa-verdict path is still honored as given. No command, subcommand, or flag was added, renamed, or removed.
Regenerated for the 1.15.0 surface: the supported-surface-at-generation-time line advanced. No contract content changed.

entries.agent_impact: The certified-template gate, doctor, and standardization report now also state each certified family’s last-verified SDK version and its delta from the current SDK, read from new per-family verification blocks on the vendored commerce surface catalog snapshot. Purely additive output: no command, flag, artifact schema, or exit-code behavior changed, and nothing that passed before fails now. A consumer may optionally read the new assembly.template_certification.freshness warning code and the catalog families[].verification blocks.

changes.summary: start/prepare-build print the accepted certified family’s freshness line; doctor reports current freshness under ready and warns with code assembly.template_certification.freshness when verification is stale or unrecorded.
Documents the identity block’s new template_certification_freshness field and Certification freshness markdown line, including the vendored-data current-SDK definition.

entries.agent_impact: The doctor command now blocks unprepared source HTML: mapped source pages with unstripped document wrappers or leftover/broken YAML frontmatter fail doctor with source_html.prep.document_wrapper / source_html.prep.frontmatter_residue errors (status blocked, next.stage collect-inputs), and source-file internal links warn as source_html.prep.internal_link_unrooted. Agents feeding raw full-document HTML into start/build must prepare the source per docs/quickstart.md "Prepare Raw HTML Source" or record wrapper_policy "preserve_document_wrappers" as an explicit adapter decision. Doctor issue codes remain governed by the ops-repo ADR-003 parity baseline, not the supported-surface manifest, so surface_version does not move.
entries.migration: Strip <!doctype>/<html>/<head>/<body> from mapped source pages, keep frontmatter as one closed leading block, and rerun campaigns-os doctor; or record wrapper_policy "preserve_document_wrappers" in the packet adapter contract for a deliberately full-document source.

changes.summary: doctor (and the doctor embedded in start/build) gained the source_html.preparation check: deterministic classification of common unprepared-source failures with actionable source_html.prep.* codes, each carrying a docs pointer; no argv change.
